name: Ethiopian Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: sign language; known works (Tamene 2016/2017, Ayansa 2021) are sociolinguistic, no word-stress description

sources.citation: Woinshet Girma. 2024. Description of Lexical Semantic Relations in Ethiopian Sign Language: Implications for Sign Language Dictionary Making. PhD dissertation, Addis Ababa University, Department of Linguistics (advisor Moges Yigezu). 211 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.1.1-2.1.3 (printed pp. 17-18) is a generic sign-language phonology overview after Brentari (handshape, location, orientation, movement, non-manual markers); the only mention of stress is a general definition: non-manual markers 'can be related to the concept of prosody. Prosody refers to linguistic elements above the segment and these include intonation, stress, tone, pitch accent, etc.' (p. 18). Nothing EthSL-specific about stress or accent anywhere in the 211 pp. Reports (p. 5) that EthSL phonology was studied by Tsehay 2012 (unpublished BA essay 'Phonetics of Ethiopian Sign Language…
Lists Tamene 2016, 2017 and Ayansa 2021 (pp. 390-391: possibly derived from or influenced by ASL); no phonological description referenced.
